title: Recover from MCP tool-call failures instead of aborting the run
body_excerpt:
## Problem (the "So What?")
Maxwell's Daemon's headline promise is letting operators "swap MCP toolsets at invocation time" and "measure each change." But today a single MCP tool-call failure is **fatal to the whole run**. In `src/agent/default.rs`, the non-bash tool path propagates the provider error with `?` (`run_non_bash_tool(...).await?` at ~line 1456, which bubbles the `provider.call(...).await?` at ~line 2344). So a spawn failure, stdio timeout, malformed/missing JSON-RPC response, a protocol-version mismatch, or a server-reported tool error aborts the entire trajectory — even at step 40 of a long, paid SWE-bench run. This is an asymmetry: a failing **bash** command becomes a recoverable observation (non-zero exit code → the agent routes around it), and a failing **model** call has `fallback_models`, but a failing **MCP** call has neither. The exact capability operators are told to lean on (swappable toolsets) is the most fragile path in the loop.

## User Story
As an agent operator running long-horizon, paid trajectories with a swapped-in MCP toolset, I want a single flaky MCP tool call to be handed back to the model as a recoverable error observation, so that one server hiccup doesn't nuke an expensive run and corrupt my measurement of the toolset.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A failed MCP tool call — process spawn failure, stdio/timeout, malformed or missing JSON-RPC response, protocol-version mismatch, or a server-reported tool error — does **not** abort the run. It is surfaced to the model as a tool observation carrying a non-zero/error indication, and the agent loop continues to the next step.
- [ ] The failure observation names the failing tool and the MCP server (redacted via the existing redaction surfaces) and gives a concise reason, so the model can retry or route to another tool.
- [ ] Each MCP failure is tagged in the trajectory with a distinct per-step marker and reason — symmetric with how chaos-injected bash timeouts are tagged (`chaos_injected: true`) — so `bench inspect`/analysis can count MCP faults separately from model behavior.
- [ ] A run-level guard prevents pathological loops: after a configurable number of consecutive failures from the same MCP tool/server (sane small default; `0`/off preserves a default rather than infinite tolerance), the run aborts **deliberately** with a clear, distinct exit code and failure category — never an opaque crash.
- [ ] The run outcome / `failure_category` distinguishes a "recoverable MCP fa

title: feat: estimate training-run cost ($) from config + GPU choice
body_excerpt:
## Problem

Users on RunPod / cloud GPUs have no upfront sense of what a training run will cost. They pick a GPU (A40 / L4 / 4090 / A100), set `epochs`, `batch_size`, `grad_accum_steps`, `image_size`, etc., and then discover hours later that the run was 3x more expensive than expected — or VRAM-OOM'd halfway through.

Today the only knob users see in `cloud/runpod/README.md` is qualitative ("A40 recommended entry tier"). We should give them a cheap pre-flight estimate.

## Proposal

A CLI / helper that takes a training config (the YAMLs in `configs/examples/`) plus a GPU choice and prints:

- estimated steps per epoch (from dataset size + `batch_size` * `grad_accum_steps`)
- estimated total steps and wall-clock time
- estimated $ cost (wall-clock * GPU $/hr)
- a VRAM-fit sanity check (warn before OOM)

Invocation idea:

```
custom-sam-peft estimate-cost configs/examples/coco_text_lora.yaml --gpu a40 --provider runpod
```

## Approach options

1. **Lookup-table + closed-form.** Bake in measured throughput (img/s) per (GPU, peft method, image_size) from a small benchmark matrix; multiply by step count. Simple, deterministic, easy to ship. Numbers drift as code changes.
2. **Quick on-device probe.** Run a 50-step warm-up on the actual hardware before the user commits to the full run. More accurate but only useful once the pod is already paid for; doesn't help pre-flight planning.
3. **Hybrid.** Ship (1) as a `cost.yaml` reference table (GPU × peft × image_size → img/s + $/hr); add an opt-in flag to run (2) for calibration.

Lean toward (1) for v1 — pre-flight is the use case that actually saves money.

## Open questions

- Where does the $/hr table live? (`cloud/runpod/pricing.yaml`? Hard-coded with a "last updated" date?) Prices drift.
- Do we support providers beyond RunPod in v1, or land RunPod-only and generalize later?
- Throughput table: do we measure it ourselves (one-time CI matrix run) or accept user-contributed numbers via PRs?
- Should this be a standalone CLI subcommand or just a section in the notebook FORM cell so non-technical users see it without leaving Jupyter?

## Scope guard

Out of scope for v1: estimating final metric quality, recommending optimal hyperparameters, multi-GPU runs.

title: [M2] Milestone 2 tracking
body_excerpt: Tracks the two remaining grant deliverables: **2-D** (SPECA × Lean integration) and **2-C** (cumulative bug & fix report). 2-A / 2-B / 2-E are already complete and only need a closeout check. ## Direction note for the EF check-in 2-D was originally worded as SPECA → Lean (generated properties converted to Lean specs). We are implementing the reverse: **Spec → Lean4**, where Lean 4 verification of the spec produces the security properties (`01e`) and the reproduction tests. This matches SPECA's existing spec→property direction and is the stronger design for our goals. title: [m17] Explore mobile version of the game
body_excerpt:
## What
Open question / exploration: should the game ship a real mobile experience, beyond the small-viewport handling tracked under #142?

## Distinct from #142
- #142 (m13) is about the existing web build not breaking on phone-sized screens — graceful degrade or punt.
- This issue is about whether mobile is a primary-target distribution channel, with all the implications: native packaging, touch input redesign, App Store / Play Store presence, save-sync, monetization model.

## Questions to answer
- **Audience fit** — is the player who'd buy this game on mobile a real audience, or a fantasy?
- **Input** — text adventures on touch are awkward. Solutions: predictive command bar, tap-to-suggest, swipe gestures, voice? Or do we lean into the terminal aesthetic and ship a soft keyboard skin?
- **Tech path** — wrap the existing web build in Capacitor / Cortex? Native rewrite? Web app with `manifest.json` and "Add to Home Screen"?
- **Cutscene cost** — pre-rendered ASCII frame files are 1–2 MB each. If every module has a cutscene, total bundle could blow past 100 MB. Need a streaming or on-demand strategy.
- **Performance** — IBM Plex Mono + per-column wipe + sweeping scanline + 12fps frame swap. Profile on a midrange Android phone.
- **Save sync** — localStorage only? iCloud / Google Play Games?
- **Pricing** — paid up front, free with IAP, free with ads (no), bundle with desktop?

## Acceptance criteria for THIS issue
- A short doc (`docs/mobile-exploration.md`) summarizing findings on the questions above
- A go / no-go recommendation with rationale
- If go: a follow-up issue for each chosen tech path, scoped roughly
- If no-go: a one-line note on the distribution plan that mobile is deferred / not pursued

## Why now
m17 is about distribution. Before promising "available on mobile" anywhere, we need to know what that costs.

title: Validate a full online-DPO training run on the trl 1.x reward_funcs path
body_excerpt:
### Context
`task='online_dpo'` (v0.71.31) adapts to the installed TRL: **judge=** (pairwise) on trl 0.19.x, and **reward_funcs=** (pointwise, the same `JudgeEvaluator` best-of-N uses) on trl 1.x — because trl 1.x removed pairwise judges and moved `OnlineDPOTrainer` to `trl.experimental.online_dpo`.

Validation so far:
- **trl 0.19.x** — a real ~1-step training run on SmolLM2-135M (rewards/kl/beta logged). ✅
- **trl 1.7.1** — the adaptation logic + `OnlineDPOTrainer(reward_funcs=[...])` **build** were validated (CI + an isolated torch-2.6 venv), but a full **training step** on the 1.x reward_funcs path was NOT exercised (the wiring test only calls `setup()`, not `train()`).

### Ask
Run a short online-DPO training run on **trl 1.x** (SmolLM2-135M, CPU or small GPU, quantization=none) with `training.online_dpo_judge` set, and confirm:
- training completes and logs a reward metric (`rewards/*`),
- the pointwise judge reward actually influences chosen/rejected selection (e.g. with the synthetic length-preferring judge, mean completion length or the judge score moves).

### Fix path
- Add a `--slow`/`trl1x`-gated test (or a manual smoke doc) that runs `OnlineDPOTrainerWrapper.train()` for a few steps on trl 1.x and asserts a `rewards/*` entry in `log_history`.
- Needs an env with trl≥1.7 + torch≥2.6 (trl 1.x OnlineDPO imports `FSDPModule`).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A metric-logged online-DPO run on trl 1.x showing the reward_funcs signal is applied.
- [ ] Documented as validated in the known-limitations / release notes.

Related: #286 (scale validation on 7B+ / real reward models).

title: Pixel Art, Bounty Drama, and Gabe Newell's First Gig
body_excerpt:
## Pixel art resurrection, AI benchmarks nobody asked for, and 80s encryption gets its revenge

- Hokusai meets MacPaint: one artist's quest to recreate Japanese woodcuts in 512x342 pixels
- OpenAI's biosafety bounty: $25k and an NDA nobody wants to sign
- Lambda calculus shows AI models can't do basic recursion
- French TV encryption from 1984 had the secret code 1337
- Gabe Newell wrote Windows 1, 2, and 3 before making video games

---

### 1-Bit Hokusai's "The Great Wave" (2023)
**TLDR**: An artist recreates Hokusai's 36 Views of Mount Fuji as 1-bit pixel art at original Macintosh resolution (512x342), using vintage hardware like a Quadra 700 and Aldus SuperPaint 3.0.

**Take**: In an era where AI can generate infinite art in seconds, someone spent years manually dithering a Japanese wave on 80s hardware. This is either the purest form of artistic devotion or the most elaborate procrastination project ever conceived.

[Article](https://www.hypertalking.com/2023/05/08/1-bit-pixel-art-of-hokusais-the-great-wave-off-kanagawa/) | [HN Discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47863570)

---

### GPT 5.5 biosafety bounty
**TLDR**: OpenAI is offering a biosafety bug bounty for GPT-5.5 with $25k in payouts, but all results are locked under NDA and cannot be published. This is a significant downgrade from their previous Kaggle bounty which had $500k in payouts.

**Take**: Nothing says 'we're serious about safety' like paying 20x less than last time and demanding everyone sign NDAs.

[Article](https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-5-bio-bug-bounty/) | [HN Discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47901734)

---

### Lambda Calculus Benchmark for AI
**TLDR**: LamBench is a benchmark of 120 pure lambda calculus programming problems. Top lab models cluster together at the top, while everyone else trails far behind. FFT remains unsolved because Church numerals make O(N log N) become O(N^2 log N).

**Take**: Finally, a benchmark that reveals what we've suspected all along: AI models are great at pattern matching but struggle with actual computation theory.

[Article](https://victortaelin.github.io/lambench/) | [HN Discussion](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47900506)

---

### Discret 11, the French TV encryption of the 80s
**TLDR**: Discret 11 was France's 1980s pay TV encryption system. Pirate decoders were built from schematics passed between friends, and the 'all free' master code was 1337 - leet before leet was cool.

**Take**: The French accidentall

title: [$30 BOUNTY] [Python] Add build diagnostic metadata tests
body_excerpt:
**Bounty:** $30 (LT)

**Area:** `build.py`

**Current state:** The build script writes diagnostic JSON metadata and encrypted `.logd` artifacts that gate PR review, but the metadata shape and logd reference behavior are not protected by focused regression tests.

**What is needed:** Add tests for diagnostic report generation so future build.py changes cannot break the JSON/logd contract expected by the GitHub diagnostic check.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Cover successful report metadata including commit id, module result summaries, and `diagnostic_logd` path.
- Cover logd generation failure populating `diagnostic_logd_error` without claiming a valid archive.
- Cover chunked or multi-file logd references if the script emits split artifacts.
- Keep tests deterministic and avoid requiring external toolchains or network access.
- Document the local command for running the new tests.

**Required validation:**
- Run the new Python test command, for example `python3 -m pytest -q` if pytest is used.
- Run `python3 build.py`.
- Include the generated `diagnostic/build-*.logd` artifact from `diagnostic/`; include the matching `diagnostic/build-*.json` if present.
- Use `.github/pull_request_template.md` for the submission.

Build Threadangle into a football-first short-form production system before the upcoming World Cup window.

The goal is not just to generate videos. The goal is to create a repeatable, fast, high-quality football content engine that can turn matchups, teams, players, storylines, and current events into postable Shorts/Reels/TikToks with strong hooks, fast cuts, clear team framing, captions, thumbnails, metadata, and analytics feedback.

title: Seeded starter bounty issues omit parent bounty reference
body_excerpt:
Parent bounty: #33

## Bug

`.github/workflows/seed-meta-issue.yml` tells contributors to reference the canonical Bug Bounty Program issue in new bounty issues, but `.github/workflows/seed-issues.yml` creates starter bounty issues without any parent/canonical bounty reference.

That makes seeded issues less traceable than manually created bounty issues and breaks the workflow guidance that new bounty issues should point back to the program instructions.

## Expected

- Before creating starter issues, the workflow should find the existing non-PR issue titled `Bug Bounty Program — How to Participate`.
- Each seeded starter issue body should include a parent bounty reference such as `Parent bounty: #33` when that canonical issue is found.
- Keep the existing `/bounty $50` marker and seeded issue acceptance criteria unchanged.

## Scope

Keep the fix focused on `.github/workflows/seed-issues.yml` plus required AI agent metadata.

title: `trace.profiler.threshold` is too coarse
body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

Please put an X between the brackets as you perform the following steps:

* [x] Check that your issue is not already filed:
      https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues
* [x] Reduce the issue to a minimal, self-contained, reproducible test case.
      Avoid dependencies to Mathlib or Batteries.
* [x] Test your test case against the latest nightly release, for example on
      https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=lean-nightly
      (You can also use the settings there to switch to “Lean nightly”)

### Description

`set_option trace.profiler.threshold` is very helpful for filtering profiles, but 1ms of resolution is too coarse; using a value of `1` doesn't capture enough data, and using a value of `0` captures way too much.

### Context

@hrmacbeth, @robertylewis and I are trying to profile and speedup `linarith`; with a threshold of `1` we miss most of the cost paid by thousands of calls to `MetaM.mkAppM`, while with a threshold of `0` the recorded data is too large and never finishes writing out to the profile file.

### Steps to Reproduce
Run
```lean
set_option trace.profiler.threshold 0.0001
set_option trace.profiler.threshold 100ns
```

**Expected behavior:** One of the above should be legal

**Actual behavior:** Neither is valid syntax, as lean options cannot hold durations or `ofScientific` literals

### Versions

4.14.0

### Additional Information

### Impact

Add :+1: to [issues you consider important](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc). If others are impacted by this issue, please ask them to add :+1: to it.

title: Refresh OCR model lineup: local-first routing, drop dead-weight engines
body_excerpt:
## Problem

The OCR engine lineup no longer reflects measured quality/cost on the owner's hardware and born-digital academic workload. Several engines are mis-ranked or dead weight:

- **DeepSeek-OCR** scores ~0.085 (socOCRbench, near dead last) yet sits in `AUTO_ENGINE_ORDER` and `_LOCAL_ENGINE_ORDER`.
- **Mistral OCR** (~0.45) is ranked as the *premium* rung above Gemini, but it is worse AND ~5x pricier than Gemini — strictly dominated.
- **Figure description** is hardwired to the Gemini API with no local-first path.
- **judge / math-recovery** defaults lean on slow/timeout-prone local models instead of the practical winner `qwen3.5:cloud`.

## Policy

Best cheap combination, **local-first → Ollama Cloud → Gemini/Mistral edge-case only**. Native PyMuPDF stays the real default for born-digital text and table *values*.

## Measured winners (owner's 64GB Mac, real workload)

- `qwen3.5:cloud` (Ollama Cloud, no extra key): ~0.57, ~49s/page, only engine to clear all 3 hard page types → practical workhorse VLM.
- Gemini 3.x: best quality (0.60-0.64) but paid + occasional empty pages → edge escalation only.
- DeepSeek-OCR / Mistral: drop from auto ladders.

## Scope (this issue)

1. New `AUTO_ENGINE_ORDER`: QWEN → GEMINI → MARKER → GLM → NOUGAT (drop DeepSeek + Mistral from auto).
2. Demote Mistral to manual-only fallback; drop DeepSeek from `_LOCAL_ENGINE_ORDER`.
3. Flip `judge_model` / `math_model` defaults to `qwen3.5:cloud`.
4. Add an LLM-friendly `MODELS.md` documenting the routing policy per sub-task (text/formula, figure description, table layout).

## Follow-ups (separate)

- Local-first figure description in `gemini_api.py`.
- Split provider identity by engine+backend+model (QWEN local vs cloud) + fix `QwenEngine.is_available()` cloud gating.

Design second opinion: Codex (gpt-5.5) — agreed with the lineup above.

title: Deploy Brain Gym to a free host and make it phone-friendly (mobile UI + persistent progress)
body_excerpt:
## Goal
Make Brain Gym deployable to a free hosting provider so it can be used from a phone browser, and ensure it works correctly and looks good on mobile. The app must remain runnable locally exactly as before (`python app.py` / `run.bat`).

## Tasks
1. **Production-ready serving.** Add a production WSGI setup (e.g., `gunicorn`) and the config to run the Flask app in production. Bind to `0.0.0.0` and read the port from the `PORT` environment variable (fall back to 5000 locally). Keep `debug=True` only for local dev.
2. **Deployment config for a free host.** Add config to deploy on a free, GitHub-integrated platform — prefer **Render** (`render.yaml`) and also include a **`Dockerfile`** + **`Procfile`** so the repo is portable to Railway/Fly.io/etc. Pin dependencies in `requirements.txt`.
3. **Fix progress persistence for ephemeral hosting.** Free hosts reset the filesystem on redeploy/sleep, which would wipe `data/progress.json` and the user's streak. Move user progress (streak, completed days, saved answers) to **browser `localStorage`** so it survives on the client, OR use a free persistent store. The local single-user experience and existing API behavior should still work; migrate gracefully and document the choice.
4. **Verify mobile responsiveness.** Confirm the UI is fully usable on a phone-sized viewport (buttons, textarea, hints, history drawer, and any new charts). Fix any overflow/tap-target issues. The layout already has some `@media` rules in `static/style.css` — build on those.
5. **Document deployment.** Add a clear "Deploy it (use from your phone)" section to the README with step-by-step instructions: connect the repo to the host, what to click, expected URL, and any environment variables. Keep it beginner-friendly.

## Constraints
- Do not break local development or existing endpoints.
- No paid services; free tiers only.
- Keep dependencies lean and pinned.
- Coordinate with the changes in #1 if both are in flight (this issue focuses on deployment + mobile + persistence; #1 focuses on features + tests).

title: [ T3 Code ] Add container, CI, and WSL environment detection to client runtime

- Return a structured `EnvironmentInfo` object with fields: runtime, platform, arch, isContainer, isCI, ciProvider, isWSL

- Docker containers are correctly identified
- Each CI provider is detected by its specific environment variable
- WSL is detected on Windows Subsystem for Linux
- When not in container or CI, isContainer and isCI are false

title: A Tool for Scrutinizing OpenGov Proposals (Don't Trust, Verify)
body_excerpt:
## Background

Last week, Kusama [Referendum 297](https://kusama.polkassembly.io/referenda/297) upgrading Relay and System chains to V1 runtimes failed due to a misconfiguration in the call and needed to be re-submitted.

There is clearly a need for a tool to ease the process for both the Fellowship and wider community to collectively verify the integrity of proposals prior to voting.

## Existing work

https://github.com/AcalaNetwork/chopsticks is well suited for dry-running proposals and verifying they do as intended. @xlc has made the most progress with this, and has provided an example script of how to 
1. Whitelist a Kusama runtime upgrade call
2. Dry-run the call, and inspect post-upgrade state using Polkadot.js

> Kusama:
>
> `npx @acala-network/chopsticks@0.9.0 xcm --relaychain kusama --parachain statemine --parachain kusama-bridge-hub`
>
> `ws://127.0.0.1:8000` for asset hub, `ws://127.0.0.1:8001` for bridge hub, `ws://127.0.0.1:8002` for kusama
>
> Open https://polkadot.js.org/apps/?rpc=ws%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A8002#/js and run this JS
>
> ```javascript
> const number = (await api.rpc.chain.getHeader()).number.toNumber()
> await api.rpc('dev_setStorage', {
>  scheduler: {
>    agenda: [
>      [
>        [number + 1], [
>          {
>            call: {
>              Inline: '0x2c0042d9642af11541927831b1795a1d47e29b2491ce8166d65076e4d63d83ccf973'
>            },
>            origin: {
>              system: 'Root'
>            }
>          }
>        ]
>      ],
>      [
>        [number + 2], [
>          {
>            call: {
>              Lookup: {
>                hash: '0xd51bacd5ea827cf48fd539d4cdd3edfc11de191ef7e3df301cebcb0cafccb5ab',
>                len: 1423658
>              }
>            },
>            origin: {
>              system: 'Root'
>            }
>          }
>        ]
>      ]
>    ]
>  }
> })
> await api.rpc('dev_newBlock', { count: 2})
> ```

## Specification (DRAFT)

A CLI that dry-runs and verifies arbitrary proposals, including those that involve XCM.
- Inputs
  - Some set of calls to dry-run (e.g. whitelist + execute referendum)
  - Expected state changes (e.g. :CODE is updated and nothing else) 
- Outputs
  - Expected state changes and unexpected state changes
  - Exposes local RPCs allowing devs to connect to and play with post-upgrade state using Polkadot.js 
- If convenient, consider dedicated subcommands to ease the process of verifying commo

title: Analytics: evaluate PostHog / Plausible / alternatives

## Goal
Understand user behavior: what features get used, where people bounce, which blog posts perform. Without analytics, we're flying blind post-launch.

## Options to evaluate

### PostHog (user's initial preference)
- Event-level analytics, sessions, funnels, feature flags, experiments
- Free tier: 1M events/month, 1 year retention
- Self-hostable
- Heavier client bundle than Plausible
- Best for: product analytics / funnel analysis

### Plausible
- Privacy-first, no cookies, lightweight (< 1 KB script)
- Simple page views + referrers
- Paid: starts at ~$9/month for 10K events
- Best for: simple traffic measurement with zero privacy baggage

### Cloudflare Web Analytics
- Free, zero setup (already on Cloudflare)
- Basic page views, geography, referrers
- Good starter; limited depth

### Datadog RUM
- Heavy, expensive — overkill for this project

## Scope
- [ ] Pick one (my lean: PostHog for depth, Plausible if privacy-first is the bigger value)
- [ ] Add to tanstack app
- [ ] Define initial events to track:
    - Page views
    - Circuit created / edited / simulated
    - Verilog exported

title: Spike: run @mysten/seal encrypt+decrypt inside a Cloudflare Worker
body_excerpt:
## Context
The Harbor HTTP API is plain `fetch` + multipart and is Worker-friendly, but `@mysten/seal` leans on WebCrypto + `@noble` curves + CPU-intensive BLS12-381. The Worker runs with `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` and `compatibility_date: 2026-05-21` (`apps/api/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc:17`), and `@mysten/sui` `^2.9.1` is already a dependency of `apps/api` (`apps/api/package.json`). Whether SEAL fits the Worker's compressed-bundle cap and CPU limit is the single highest-risk unknown gating the entire private-memory workstream (roadmap "The key runtime unknown (must spike early)" + §1 spike row).

## Goal / user story
As an engineer, I want a throwaway Worker that imports `@mysten/seal`, encrypts one blob and decrypts it back, so we can decide WHERE encryption runs (Worker vs queue consumer vs Node CLI/MCP) before investing in `HarborClient`/`seal.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A minimal Worker (or `apps/api` test entry) imports `@mysten/seal` + `@mysten/sui/keypairs/ed25519`, and encrypts a small (<10KB) `Uint8Array` against a Seal policy id on Sui testnet, returning ciphertext.
- [ ] The same Worker builds a `SessionKey` + `seal_approve` PTB and decrypts the ciphertext back to the original bytes (round-trip asserted byte-equal).
- [ ] `wrangler deploy --dry-run` (or a real deploy) reports the compressed bundle size, recorded against the Workers size cap; CPU ms for one encrypt+decrypt is noted.
- [ ] A written finding recommends where encryption runs (Worker / queue consumer / Node-only) backed by the bundle + CPU numbers.
- [ ] If the Worker busts limits, the fallback (encrypt in the queue consumer or Node CLI/MCP) is documented so the Harbor client/encrypted-path issues target the right runtime.

## Implementation notes
- Add `@mysten/seal` to a scratch package or `apps/api` (do NOT keep it in the prod bundle if the spike fails). `@mysten/sui` is already present.
- You need a real `seal_policy_id` on Sui **testnet** — create one via Harbor (a bucket create yields a Seal policy) or reuse the `seal-docs.wal.app` example policy; the demo sample target already points there (`CONTEXTMEM_DEMO_SAMPLE_TARGET` in `wrangler.jsonc`).
- `SessionKey` requires an Ed25519 signer: `decodeSuiPrivateKey(suiprivkey1...)` → `Ed25519Keypair`. Use `SuiGrpcClient` (already used in `packages/walrus/src/proof.ts`/`history.ts`/`resolve.ts`) for the `seal_approve` devInspect.

title: [RFC] Deterministic Reward Inference and VLM Reward Model Support
body_excerpt:
## Motivation

verl-omni's reward framework supports two reward model pathways:

- **DisRM** (discriminative): text-only, subject to floating-point nondeterminism, **cannot handle visual input**
- **GenRM** (generative): supports VLM Vision API, but **sampling params hardcoded** (`temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8`) in every `/v1/chat/completions` request, with no seed control for reproducibility

Three gaps:

1. **No floating-point determinism** — flash attention split-K, CUDA matmul, NCCL all-reduce, MoE routing can all produce floating-point variation across RM inference runs
2. **No configurable GenRM sampling** — GenRM's hardcoded per-request params bypass RM rollout config; users cannot control sampling behavior or provide seed for reproducibility
3. **No VLM scoring path** — enabling RM without a custom reward function has no built-in visual scoring entry point, requiring manual configuration

## Design

Add `deterministic` and `seed` fields under `reward_model` in YAML config:

- **`deterministic=true`** — full determinism applied to RM actors via `enable_full_determinism(seed)` + `PYTHONHASHSEED` injected via `runtime_env`; `seed` propagated to GenRM HTTP requests (same seed + same input → same output, controlled pseudorandom)
- **`deterministic=false`** — full randomness, `seed` not propagated
- **Sampling params** (`temperature/do_sample/top_k/top_p`) are entirely user-configured in YAML under `rollout`, the `deterministic` flag does not override them

### 1. Floating-point determinism

RM inference uses `name=vllm` servers (`vLLMReplica` + `vLLMHttpServer`). When `deterministic=true`, monkey-patch `vLLMReplica.launch_servers()` with `_DeterministicServerProxy` which does two things:

**Env vars injection** — `PYTHONHASHSEED` must be set before Python process startup, so it is injected into RM actor `runtime_env`. Rollout actors remain unaffected (`is_reward_model` guard).

**Server class swap** — Replace `vLLMHttpServer` with `_DeterministicRMHttpServer(vLLMHttpServer)` subclass, which calls verl's `enable_full_determinism(seed)` in `_post_init`. This covers all in-process determinism: env vars (`CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`, `FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE`, `NCCL_PROTO`), Python/NumPy/PyTorch seeds, deterministic algorithms, cuDNN config.

| Setting | Set by |
|---|---|
| `PYTHONHASHSEED=str(seed)` | `runtime_env` (before process startup) |
| `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:16:8` | `enable_full_determinism` (in-proce

title: Hub: repeatable bounty board
body_excerpt:
Sub-issue of #1602 (Hub World epic).

## Why
Hub quests are mostly one-shot. A bounty board offers a renewable reason to play: rotating daily/weekly fetch & objective bounties that pay crystals/items.

## What to build
- A bounty-board interactable that offers N rotating bounties (seeded by date, like daily/weekly challenges) drawn from templates (collect X items, talk to Y, win a quick battle). Claim → track → turn in for crystals.

title: Add Playwright e2e coverage for the Decline Applicant flow

title: Bounty system: wanted status, bounty hunters, criminal record
body_excerpt:
## What
When the player accumulates crimes, they become wanted. Bounty hunters pursue them. Faction patrols attack on sight.

**Bounty mechanics:** Crimes tracked per faction. When crimes exceed a threshold, player is wanted in that faction's territory. Bounty amount = crime severity × faction power. Bounty hunters have their own ship classes and AI — pursue the player across systems.

**Hiding reputation:** Player can pay off bounties at neutral stations (expensive). Letting time pass reduces notoriety but not crimes. Changing identity (new ship, false papers) is a major operation.

**Smuggling:** Blockade running without being caught. Scan evasion mechanics. Contraband detected during docking scans — bribes, smuggling compartments, or fast talk.

**Dependencies:** #35 (reputation), #29 (landed combat — bounty hunters on station)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Bounty generated from crime record
- [ ] Bounty hunters pursue across systems
- [ ] Paying bounty removes wanted status
- [ ] Smuggling mechanics: scan evasion, compartments
- [ ] `tests/wave_3_bounty.gd` passes

title: Clarify scope and acceptance criteria for Dart port bounty
body_excerpt:
Hi maintainers,

I’m interested in working on the Dart port mentioned in the Monero Bounties post:

https://bounties.monero.social/posts/166/1-000m-port-the-haveno-api-library-from-typescript-to-dart

Before starting implementation, I’d like to confirm the expected scope and acceptance criteria publicly.

Proposed scope:
- Create a Dart package equivalent to the core `haveno-ts` client API.
- Generate or maintain Dart gRPC/protobuf bindings for the Haveno daemon API.
- Implement a typed client with the main flows used in the current `haveno-ts` README sample:
  - connect to daemon
  - get balances
  - get payment accounts
  - get offers / my offers
  - take offer
  - disconnect
- Add focused tests for generated bindings/client wrappers and mockable gRPC behavior.
- Add README usage examples and setup instructions.

Questions:
1. Is this scope enough for the bounty, or is a full feature-for-feature port expected?
2. Should the Dart package live in a new repository, a fork, or under the Haveno organization?
3. Which maintainer should review/ACK the work?
4. Are there any existing contributors already working on this?
5. What exact criteria should be met for payout eligibility?

I won’t start implementation until there is public concept ACK from the project/maintainers so the work is aligned with Haveno’s expectations.

title: CI issue 2310 validation tests use Windows-only subprocess paths
body_excerpt:
## Bug
`tests/test_issue2310_package_validation.py` uses Windows-only backslash paths inside subprocess calls:

- `sys.path.insert(0, r'bounties\issue-2310')`
- `bounties\issue-2310\validate_bounty_2310.py`

This passes on Windows, but on the Linux CI runner those backslashes are literal path characters. The broad `test` job then fails because the subprocess imports the wrong `src` module and cannot open the validator script.

## Steps to reproduce
On a Linux checkout of `main`:

```bash
python -B -m pytest -q tests/test_issue2310_package_validation.py --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider
```

Current CI failure symptoms from the `test` job include:

```text
AttributeError: module 'src' has no attribute 'CRTPatternGenerator'
python: can't open file '.../bounties\\issue-2310\\validate_bounty_2310.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

## Expected
The test should import the issue-2310 package and run `validate_bounty_2310.py` on both Windows and Linux.

## Actual
Windows path separators are passed to Linux subprocesses, so the package import and validator invocation fail in CI.

## Fix
Opened PR #5631 to build both subprocess paths with `pathlib` instead of hard-coded Windows separators:

https://github.com/Scottcjn/Rustchain/pull/5631

## Local validation on Windows
- `python -B -m pytest -q tests/test_issue2310_package_validation.py --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider` -> 2 passed
- `python -B -m py_compile tests/test_issue2310_package_validation.py`
- `git diff --check`

title: Payment intent should reject unsupported currencies
body_excerpt:

## Problem

`createPaymentIntent()` currently returns `payload.currency` directly when a caller provides it. The mock Stripe intent defaults to `usd`, but it does not reject unsupported, empty, or non-string currency values.

## Impact

Unsupported payment currency values can enter the payment flow and later reach a real payment provider integration, where they may fail unexpectedly or create inconsistent accounting assumptions.

Payment intent creation should accept the default `usd` behavior and valid `usd` input, while rejecting unsupported, empty, or non-string currencies with `400 Bad Request`.

Keep the fix limited to payment currency validation and error handling. Add regression tests proving unsupported currencies are rejected and the default/valid USD behavior still works.

title: [ADR] Static -- @assert: annotation linting (W025)
body_excerpt:
What
A new warning rule, W025 assertion-malformed, that scans for -- @assert: comments in SQL files and flags any whose predicate doesn't parse. The rule does not execute the assertion — execution belongs to dbt tests, a downstream runner, or a follow-up companion tool.

Why
sql-sop catches dangerous SQL. It says nothing about whether the data the query returns is sane. That gap gets filled today by:

dbt tests — only if you use dbt
Great Expectations / Soda — new vendor, DB connection required
nothing, which is most teams
-- @assert: comments are the lightest possible way to write a data assertion next to the query that produces the data. The problem is that nothing currently reads them, so people write whatever they feel like. By owning the syntax, sql-sop makes them machine-checkable. Execution is somebody else's problem.

Grammar (v1)
-- @assert: <predicate>
predicate := row_count <op> <int>
           | unique(<col>)
           | not_null(<col>)
           | <col> <op> <literal>
op       := = | != | < | <= | > | >=
col      := <bare> ( . <bare> )?           e.g. weight, users.batch_id
bare     := [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
literal  := <int> | <float> | '<string>' | "<string>"
Examples that parse:

-- @assert: row_count > 0
-- @assert: row_count >= 100
-- @assert: unique(batch_id)
-- @assert: unique(orders.batch_id)
-- @assert: not_null(weight)
-- @assert: weight > 0
-- @assert: status = 'paid'
Examples the rule fires on:

-- @assert: row_count
-- @assert: row_count > zero
-- @assert: unique batch_id
-- @assert: weight is positive
Whitespace
Tolerant. Extra whitespace anywhere between --, @assert, :, and the predicate is fine. Leading indentation on the comment line is fine. Trailing whitespace before end-of-line is ignored. All three of these read the same to the rule:

-- @assert: unique(id)
--   @assert:   unique(id)
    -- @assert: unique(id)
Identifiers — what's in, what's out
In for v1: bare identifiers and one level of qualification — weight, users.batch_id.

Out for v1: quoted identifiers in any dialect.

standard SQL "batch-id"
T-SQL [batch id]
MySQL `batch_id`
Reason: quoted identifiers are uncommon in assertion targets (you usually assert on clean column names), the three quote styles each need separate handling, and getting it wrong is a false-positive that costs every downstream user. Easy to add in v1.1 if a real user asks.

Scope discipline
Hard line, per GOVERNANCE.md: the rule does not execute anything. No DB connection. No credentials. Pu

title: Planning optimization: cross-goal trajectory caching (+ evaluate cost-based planning)
body_excerpt:
### Problem
Between independent goals, identical start→goal moves are **re-planned from scratch** every time. The repo already has planning caches, but none reuse trajectories across goals:
- **Planner-object cache** (`base_stages.py:412`) — reuses solver instances per task; not a trajectory cache.
- **Plan-replay cache** (`core/plan_cache.py`) — **single-entry**, scoped to one dry-run→execute round-trip, keyed on `(goal JSON, gripper)`. It's a *consistency* mechanism (execute exactly what you previewed), not a cross-goal *performance* cache.

Planning is the dominant latency (see prior latency investigation — goal→motion is planning-bound). Caching repeated motions is the win.

### Part B — Cross-goal trajectory caching (implement)
Reuse a stored trajectory for a repeated start→goal pair instead of re-planning. Two candidate homes — **decide during this work, don't pre-commit**:
- `moveit_ros/trajectory_cache` (upstream warehouse: DB-backed, constraint-aware, fuzzy start-state matching) — maintained, more setup.
- Extend the existing `PlanCache` from single-entry to keyed multi-entry on `(start pose, goal pose, gripper)` — lighter, in-repo, but we own the matching logic.

**Key constraint — start-state matching:** a cached trajectory is only replayable if the robot is actually at its start state within tolerance. This fails *safe*: MoveIt's `trajectory_execution.allowed_start_tolerance` (~0.01 rad, on by default) already rejects a stale-start replay **before motion** (documented in `plan_cache.py:85-91`), so a mismatch loudly re-plans rather than jumping. Lean on this rather than reinventing the check.

### Part A — Cost-based planning (evaluate, may not implement)
Today every stage plans with `max_solutions=1` and **no cost term** (`base_stages.py:671`) — it takes the *first* valid plan, not the best. MTC supports `stage.setCostTerm(...)` (built-in `PathLength`, `TrajectoryDuration`, `Clearance`) + `plan(max_solutions=N>1)` to keep the cheapest of several.
- **Evaluate** the latency/quality tradeoff: this makes planning *slower* (generates N plans) for *smoother/shorter* trajectories. Document whether it's worth it; implementation optional.
- **Note the interaction with B:** if cost-based planning produces meaningfully better trajectories, the combination is "plan the good one once (A), cache and replay forever (B)" — A's cost paid once, B's speed thereafter. The evaluation should report on this so we know *what* to cache.

### Deliverables
1. Cross-goal

TINYGRAD & INFRA * Expect potential refactoring of concatenation operations in tinygrad — George Hotz is questioning the necessity of the `CAT` operation, suggesting it might be redundant and replaceable by other operations like `VCAT`, `PTRCAT`, `VECTORIZE`, and `MSTACK`. title: Landing page v2: let the USPs carry the page
body_excerpt:
## Context

Maintainer review of the live site (2026-07-06): layout and tone are right — simple, plain, keep that character. But the page should make the *why use this* case harder. Full gap analysis against the maintainer's USP list exists (session work, 2026-07-06); the measured facts below are verified.

## The four gaps to close

1. **Cost framing.** "Pay for usage, not a subscription" exists as a reason, but the numbers are buried and the subscription contrast is missing. Target framing (measured, honest): subscription dictation tools run ~$12–15/month (no competitor named on the page); the maintainer's all-day heavy use — ~25 h of audio/month, measured over the last 6 months from the local archive — costs about **$3/month** at Soniox's $0.12/h; lighter regular use lands around a dollar; the Groq path is free.
2. **Python-script transparency.** The word "Python" does not appear on the page. State it plainly: a single Python script, not an installed product — lean, fully readable, easy to modify (see 4); trade-off is a terminal window instead of a GUI (a VISION non-goal anyway). Natural spot: the get-started/audience block, or a sixth reason.
3. **Feature breadth.** There is no features section, so the "this actually does a lot" impression never forms. Add ONE compact section (after the lineup, before privacy): verbatim/polished modes, runtime API switching, recognition vocabulary, push-to-talk (currently mentioned nowhere), history archive of every recording + transcript, retry + crash-safety net, "extend it by telling your AI coding agent".
4. **Free path from "try" to "use".** Groq's free tier is generous and permanent (2,000 requests/day, up to 8 h audio/day — verified 2026-07-06). It can be framed as a real way to *run* the tool, keeping the honest asterisk that the German-quality anchor is the paid Soniox default.

## Hard constraints

- **Docs-first rule stands** (#75: every statement traces to README/VISION/CHANGELOG, no invented numbers). The cost figures above must land in README **first** (as measured maintainer experience with prices per provider pricing pages, dated), then on the page. Same for push-to-talk phrasing etc. — page follows docs.
- **Vocabulary, not "replacements".** The tool has a recognition vocabulary (context terms that improve recognition upstream). It has NO post-hoc find-and-replace — verified in code 2026-07-06. The page must name it truthfully.
- Soniox note worth reflecting in setup-facing text: free starting credits

title: Epic: Passport (visited shops)
body_excerpt:
The **passport** turns "marking shops visited" into the emotional core of having an account: a known denominator (*X of N shops*), a map that literally fills in, and neighborhood-level progress. It builds directly on the `user_visits` primitive already shipped on the `visited-passport` branch.

A series of improvements on top of that primitive:

- [ ] Visited toggle + count primitive (**already shipped** on `visited-passport`)
- [ ] Color the map — light up visited pins
- [ ] Anonymous-first visited state (shared anon layer with favorites)
- [ ] Signup backfill — first-run "which of these have you been to?" checklist
- [ ] Neighborhood progress ("5 of 7 in Lawrenceville")
- [ ] Milestone moments — the cheap, computed version
- [ ] Shareable passport — OG image / public passport page

The count and the filling-in map are the co-equal emotional cores; everything else compounds on them.

## Out of scope
Friends / social graph, public profiles, shared feeds, cross-user leaderboards, crowd ratings, any paid passport (per `BLIND_SPOTS.md` #4). The Coffee Week seasonal view is a later view on top of this data.

---

### ⚠️ Known tension to resolve
The shipped primitive is **login-gated**, but the "anonymous-first" improvement reworks how the already-shipped toggle stores state so marking visited doesn't require signup. The map coloring and signup backfill lean on that shared anon state.

The README hero currently shows a placeholder line ("A demo GIF is on the way..."). Recording the GIF is the last thing missing from
  a complete v1 README.

  ## What to capture

  The end-to-end flow:

  1. Open Hunty's Tasks page with a task ready to run
  2. Hand off the prompt to Claude (Claude in Chrome)
  3. Watch Claude scan a LinkedIn search or careers page
  4. Cut to the kanban filling up with new jobs

  Bonus: capture the duplicate-detection moment (Check URL) and a "Saved" badge appearing.

  ## Specs

  - **Width:** 600–800px (cropped tight, not full-screen)
  - **Length:** 8–20 seconds
  - **File size:** under 5MB (GitHub caps at 10MB)

  ## Recommended tools

  - [Kap](https://getkap.co/) — free
  - [ScreenStudio](https://www.screen.studio/) — auto-zooms on clicks, very polished
  - [CleanShot X](https://cleanshot.com/) — paid, clean output

  ## Hosting

  Drag-drop the file into a draft GitHub issue (don't post it). GitHub uploads to its CDN and gives you a
  `https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/...` URL. Use that URL in the README — keeps the repo lean.

title: [FEATURE] Section 2001: Implement missing subsections (d), (e), (f)
body_excerpt:
## Context

Section 2001 currently implements the core estate tax calculation (subsections a, b, c) but is missing three additional subsections that handle special cases and coordination rules.

## Location

**File**: `src/TaxCode/Section2001.lean`  
**Lines**: 194-196 (TODOs at end of file)

## Missing Features

### IRC § 2001(d): Gift tax paid by spouse

**Description**: Adjustments when the decedent's spouse paid gift tax on prior gifts.

**Code comment**:
```lean
-- TODO: Implement adjustments for gift tax paid by spouse (IRC §2001(d))
```

**What's needed**:
- Model joint gifts and split gifts
- Calculate adjustments to tentative tax
- Coordinate with § 2513 (split gift elections)

### IRC § 2001(e): Coordination with § 2513 and § 2035

**Description**: Special rules for coordinating estate tax with gift-splitting elections and gifts made within 3 years of death.

**Code comment**:
```lean
-- TODO: Implement coordination of sections 2513 and 2035 (IRC §2001(e))
```

**What's needed**:
- § 2513: Gift-splitting between spouses
- § 2035: Gifts made within 3 years of death included in estate
- Adjustments to calculation when both apply

### IRC § 2001(f): Valuation of gifts

**Description**: Rules for valuing prior taxable gifts for purposes of the estate tax calculation.

**Code comment**:
```lean
-- TODO: Implement valuation of gifts logic (IRC §2001(f))
```

**What's needed**:
- Use gift tax return values (not date-of-death values)
- Handle cases where gift values have changed
- Model finality of gift tax valuations

## Suggested Approach

1. **Extend data structures**: Add fields to capture spouse gift tax info, split gift elections, etc.
2. **New calculation functions**: `apply_section_2001_d`, `coordinate_2513_and_2035`, `value_prior_gifts`
3. **Update main function**: Integrate new subsections into `section2001_b_computation`
4. **Add theorems**: Verify adjustments preserve tax law requirements

## Impact

These are **optional enhancements** - the core estate tax logic is complete. However, these subsections are needed for:
- Estates with substantial lifetime gifts
- Joint returns with split gifts
- Gifts made near death

## Priority

**LOW** - Nice to have, but core functionality is complete

## References

- IRC § 2001(d), (e), (f)
- Current implementation: Lines 113-116 (main computation)
- Related: § 2513 (gift splitting), § 2035 (3-year rule)

title: When they win #28: review the site's framing (drought → champions)
body_excerpt:
A todo for whenever the Yankees win their next title. The whole site is built on the "they're due / drought" premise, so a championship isn't just a data bump — it should be a deliberate editorial review. **By design, the weekly updater does NOT auto-detect a title** (mis-flipping the narrative would be worse than a manual edit), so this is intentionally a human pass.

## 1. Data / constants — `scripts/update_data.py`
- `LAST_TITLE_YEAR` → the new championship year
- `TOTAL_TITLES` 27 → 28
- `TITLES` → append the new year
- `TITLES_BY_DECADE` → increment the matching decade's count
- `CHASING_NUMBER` 28 → 29
- `HISTORICAL_DROUGHTS` → close out the `"2009–present"` entry with its final length; the drought is over, so `drought_seasons` resets to 0
- `DROUGHT_YEARS` → the title year is now a WS *win*, not a drought year — decide whether the section becomes "the seasons it took" or gets reframed
- Re-run `python3 scripts/update_data.py` (auto-syncs the inline fallback + redeploys)

## 2. Copy / narrative — `index.html`
Every section currently argues the drought. Review each:
- **Hero** — "They're Due", the headline drought number, "0 rings in the longest drought since the dynasty" all need rewriting (celebration vs. retrospective).
- **The 2009 Cliff** — there's a newer last title now; reframe or repurpose.
- **The Drought Years** — the new year breaks the "good enough for October, never enough" thesis.
- **The Near-Misses** — context shifts from "so close" to "before they finally broke through".
- **Why Now** — becomes "they did it" / how the window paid off.
- **Closer** — "They're *due.*" and the giant gold **28** flip to a payoff; the statistical "due" case is now fulfilled.

## 3. Decide the site's fate (the real question)
Pick a direction before editing:
- **(a) Celebration/coda** — keep the structure, add a "the wait is over" ending and re-point the argument.
- **(b) Retrospective** — rewrite to "how the drought finally ended," archiving the tension as backstory.
- **(c) Freeze + archive** — snapshot the current "they're due" version (it only makes sense pre-#28) and start fresh.

## 4. Small cleanups
- Footer `© 2026 MQ` year
- Accent usage (gold currently = "ring they don't have"; may want to lean into it as "ring they got")
- Photo set may want a championship image in the hero/closer

_Filed at the user's request as a reminder; no action until it actually happens. ⚾_

title: Epic: Paid Unlock MVP
body_excerpt:
## Summary

Create a lean paid-unlock system for CozyBlock built around a single Gumroad purchase, Netlify-hosted backend functions, and local entitlement persistence in the app.

## Locked Product Contract
- one Gumroad product: `Unlock Full Game`
- one purchase unlocks all premium worlds, including future premium worlds
- `World 0` and `World 1` are free by default
- the free/premium split remains configurable in content data
- no accounts or email restore in v1
- restore uses a user-saved restore code
- restore codes can be reused without limit
- claim is automatic from Gumroad redirect data
- refunds/revocations are not handled in v1
- hosting and backend live on Netlify

## Child Issues
- [ ] Define Premium Content Contract In Level Data: https://github.com/rschroed/CozyBlock/issues/28
- [ ] Make Navigation And Progression Paywall-Aware: https://github.com/rschroed/CozyBlock/issues/29

## Launch Checklist
- free players can play `World 0` and `World 1`
- premium worlds show a paywall instead of loading directly for free players

title: Threads - (Dev Bounty: $750)
body_excerpt:
**Status: needs mobile and desktop visual design**

# Background

Threads are one of our top requested features. A common desire on chat platform, akin to breakout rooms for specific sub-conversations, threads are generally considered to be “sub-channels” that sit inside a larger channel. Threads typically have a unique name and a starting message, however the latter should be viewed as optional.


We should avoid diverging from industry standard. Nor should we think of threads as a buildup to forums. Both serve different niches. Threads allow for quickly zooming in on a specific message during an active conversation. Forums create hubs for specific types of conversations. While the two products may intersect at a later point, as a MVP to meet user needs rapidly, we should focus our efforts on just implementing a standard “threads feature”


# Product needs

All designs below (except instance level safety) should be treated as strong suggestions. If you feel you have a better design, we encourage you to explore it, but please understand that if it is not to the team’s liking, we may not accept the end result. Instance level safety designs are requirements.


TLDR → Threads are sub-channels. They inherit a large amount of base design and UX from channels. There are specific nuances in the API, database structure, and UX for them, but broadly, they should be treated as channels. 


## Initiation - (Desktop)

### Starting a thread

* Users should be able to create a thread in any text based channel via three methods:
  * Hovering over an existing message should display a “thread” icon in the context menu. The thread icon should be in between the reply and the forward icons. A tooltip should appear above with “Start new thread”
    * If the message is already the start of a thread, this tooltip should instead read “Join thread”, and enter the user into the thread. They should not be able to start a secondary thread.
  * When right clicking a message or hitting the hamburger icon on a message, a “Start new thread” button should be there.
    * If the message is already the start of a thread, this tooltip should instead read “Join thread”, and enter the user into the thread. They should not be able to start a secondary thread.
* “/thread” in the chat box should allow you to also initiate a thread

$50

The template should default to the same `/bounty $50` marker used by the seeded bounty issues and the program instructions.

title: Payment creation should reject non-positive amounts (YfengJ reissue via #743)
body_excerpt:
Parent bounty: #743

Reissue of #6437 for participation under parent bounty #743.

## Bug

`POST /api/payments` accepts invalid `amount` values because the payment controller forwards `req.body` directly into `paymentService.createPaymentIntent`. The service then stores `payload.amount` without checking that it is a positive number.

## Reproduction

1. Send `POST /api/payments` with `{ amount: -100, currency: "usd" }`.
2. Observe that the route creates a payment intent with a negative amount.
3. Send `{ amount: 0, currency: "usd" }` or `{ amount: "free", currency: "usd" }`.
4. These invalid values are not rejected before reaching the service.

## Expected behavior

Payment creation should validate the request body before calling the service:

- `amount` must be a positive number greater than 0.
- `currency` should be an optional 3-letter code with a safe default.
- Invalid payment bodies should return the existing `{ success: false, message }` response shape with `400 Bad Request`.

## Scope

Keep the fix limited to payment creation validation and focused route-level regression coverage. Do not change unrelated payment provider behavior.

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

title: Paid and Organic Campaign Measurement
body_excerpt:
> **Migrated issue.** Originally filed as moldovancsaba/mvp-factory-control#798 (created 2026-05-10). Moved to `moldovancsaba/messmass` on 2026-07-03 as part of the board consolidation (all open board work now lives in this repo, per docs/PROJECT_MANAGEMENT.md).

---

## Objective

Measure paid and organic campaign performance in one reporting model so sponsor impact can be evaluated holistically.

## Unified Context

Relo Metrics explicitly calls out paid plus organic measurement as part of a complete sponsorship view. `{messmass}` currently leans on organic and operational metrics, leaving paid amplification less integrated.

## Problem

Campaign performance is incomplete if paid amplification and organic reach are reported separately or not connected. Without one model, sponsor value discussions miss a major part of the media mix.

## Goal

Unify paid and organic campaign evidence in the same attribution and reporting layer.

## Scope

### In Scope

- data model for paid campaign signals alongside organic signals
- shared attribution view across paid, organic, and tracked-link outcomes
- reporting outputs for combined and separated campaign performance
- governance for labeling which metrics are platform-provided versus internally derived

### Out of Scope

- full ad-buying or campaign execution tooling
- every ad-platform integration in the first version

## Execution Prompt

Focus on holistic measurement and clear labeling. The product should help users understand total campaign contribution without obscuring what was organic, paid, or inferred.

## Constraints

- paid and organic metrics must remain distinguishable
- attribution assumptions must be explicit
- the first version should target the highest-value integration path

## Acceptance Checks

- [ ] paid and organic inputs can exist in one campaign-performance model
- [ ] reports can show combined and separated views
- [ ] attribution assumptions are documented in-product
- [ ] users can evaluate total sponsor campaign contribution

## Risks

- platform metric mismatch can complicate comparisons
- users may overinterpret blended performance without clear labels

## Delivery Artifact

A unified paid plus organic campaign measurement model for `{messmass}`.

## Developer Notes

Research basis: Relo Metrics.

title: Polls - (Dev Bounty: $500)
body_excerpt:
# Background

Polls have two purposes:
1. Quick and easy single selection polls to quickly gather thoughts
2. Ranked choice polls that help to collect detailed feedback. 


We want to be able to support both needs, as detailed below.

# User Stories

## Megan - Group DM Member (simple poll)

Megan is in a group chat with her friends. She wants to be able to quickly ask folks which dress of hers looks best. To do so, she creates a poll. In the poll creation menu, she is able to to upload images and write text next next to them. She is able to set a title and a duration. She also gets to toggle ranked voting and anonymous responses. Finally, she has the option to allow people to select custom responses. 

In this case, she creates a simple poll with no ranked voting and no custom responses. Once Megan hits confirm, a poll appears in the chat. 

### Desktop
On desktop, Megan's friends see a poll appear with each (smaller) image / text option. The header has the title and Megan's profile picture. 

The results are hidden from them until they hit submit. Clicking on each image brings it up bigger with the text as a caption. Users are able to click left or right arrows or use their arrow keys to go between options. Double clicking on the image selects it as the selected choice. They are able to undo that choice by double clicking again. 

Once something is double clicked, a new button on the poll will appear to show results. Results will be shown in order of most to least voted. Next to each option, a pfp of the voters. If the friend clicks on an option again, the same popup is shown, this time with the pfp of the voters in the bottom corner.

After the allotted time, the poll closes. Votes become viewable to all users, and no more votes can be accepted.   

### Mobile
Very similar experience, except in this case, if images are included, clicking on an option pulls up an image carousal that can be swiped through. Holding down on an selects it as an option. 

### Ranked Choice
Ranked choice is similar, except you can select multiple options, It shows you the order selected in both the image carasoul and in the chat. When you view the votes, you get shown the first place selections in order. You can click a button to then see the order changing when 2nd choice votes are added, then 3rd place votes, etc...

title: [FEATURE] Tablica zleceń — bounty board w osadach
body_excerpt:
## Koncept — co widzi gracz

W każdej większej osadzie (lokacja z tagiem osady / safe_for_rest) wisi **tablica zleceń** z 2–3 aktywnymi kontraktami:

- „Wilki nękają gospodarstwo pod Wilczburgiem" (łowiecki)
- „Zaginął kupiec na trakcie do Wachstein" (śledztwo / eskorta)
- „Dostarcz paczkę do młyna przed zmrokiem" (dostawa, limit czasu z systemu podróży)

Zasady:
- Kontrakt jest **krótki (1–3 sceny)**, niezależny od głównego planu GM — nie dotyka `gm_plan_json`.
- Nagroda: złoto + reputacja regionu (istniejący system reputacji per-region, #1099).
- Tablica odświeża się na cooldownie (mechanizm jak `character_dungeon_runs`).
- Gracz może mieć ograniczoną liczbę aktywnych kontraktów naraz (start: 2 — wartość do tuningu).
- Kontrakty wypełniają pustkę „pomiędzy" beatami kampanii — dziś jedyny farmable content to lochy.

## Zarządzanie — co widzi admin

- Tabela **szablonów kontraktów** (typ: łowiecki / eskorta / dostawa / śledztwo) — edycja w Kuźni lub przez Smart Entry.
- LLM losuje szablon i ubiera go w lokalny kontekst: nazwy z okolicznych heksów, NPC z regionu, aktualne wydarzenia.
- Monitor kampanii pokazuje, jakie kontrakty gracz przyjął i w jakim są stanie.

## Dlaczego pasuje do gry

Travel system (FAZA PT), reputacja regionalna i infrastruktura cooldownów już istnieją — to w ~80% sklejenie gotowych klocków. Naturalny kanał dystrybucji: plotki w karczmach (issue siostrzane).

## Proces wdrożenia

title: Payment intent should default currency to uppercase USD
body_excerpt:
Parent bounty: #743

## Problem
`createPaymentIntent()` defaults payment currency to lowercase `usd`, while the Prisma `Payment` model defaults to uppercase `USD` and ISO 4217 currency codes are conventionally uppercase.

## Expected behavior
- Missing currency should default to `USD`.
- Explicit currencies should still be preserved.
- Add focused service coverage for both paths.

## Scope
Keep the fix limited to `apps/api/src/services/paymentService.js` plus a focused service test.

Reissue of #5348 because that issue is limited to its creator.

title: Payment currency should normalize to lowercase before processing
body_excerpt:
Parent bounty: #743

## Bug
paymentService.createPaymentIntent stores payload.currency as-is. Payment processors such as Stripe expect lowercase currency codes, so an uppercase value like USD can fail downstream when the Stripe integration is active.

## Expected behavior
Normalize explicit currency values to lowercase before returning or forwarding the payment intent payload. Missing currency should continue to default to usd.

## Scope
Keep the fix limited to payment currency normalization and focused service coverage.

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

# Phase 6 — Community & Launch (kickoff)

Phase 5 closed at 2026-06-14 03:00 CT (10/10 production-hardening milestones merged). This issue scopes Phase 6.

## Goal

Move AI Harness from "fully featured, production-grade Go harness" → "the reference implementation of Harness as Code with real adopters."

## Tracks

### 6.1 Documentation site (mdBook → htek.dev mirror)
- [ ] `docs/getting-started.md` — 5-min quickstart, end-to-end, real provider
- [ ] `docs/concepts/` — tools, hooks, delegation, scripting, evals (one page each)
- [ ] `docs/guides/` — first agent, governance with hooks, testing with evals, copilot API integration, migration from LangChain/CrewAI
- [ ] `docs/reference/` — config schema, Starlark builtins, hook events catalog, full CLI reference
- [ ] `docs/examples/` — runnable: simple-chatbot, code-reviewer, governed-agent, self-extending
- [ ] `docs/deploy/` — link out to `deploy/` recipes (5.10) with production checklist

### 6.2 Launch sequence (htek.dev / community)
- [ ] v1.0.0 release tag once docs + examples land
- [ ] "Introducing Harness as Code" launch post (htek.dev) — vendor-bias framing, Pi comparison, why-Go
- [ ] Post to r/golang, Hacker News, Go Discord
- [ ] "Building Governed AI Agents in Go" tutorial (htek.dev + video)

### 6.3 Reference content
- [ ] "Why I Built Another Agent Framework" — awareness
- [ ] "Hook-Based AI Governance in Go" — education
- [ ] "Migrating from LangChain to Harness as Code" — adoption
- [ ] "Production Agent Patterns" — example configs

### 6.4 Future extension points (deferred to post-launch)
- Plugin packages (Go modules) — import external tool packages
- Hook packs — reusable governance bundles as MD artifacts
- Harness inheritance/overlays
- VS Code extension — config validation + Starlark highlighting

## Sequencing

1. **Week 1:** docs/getting-started + concepts/tools + concepts/hooks + one full example (governed-agent).

- [ ] Customer chọn reward.
- [ ] Hệ thống kiểm tra reward active.
- [ ] Hệ thống refresh điểm active.
- [ ] Hệ thống kiểm tra Customer đủ điểm.
- [ ] Hệ thống trừ điểm theo FIFO.
- [ ] Hệ thống tạo Redemption status `AVAILABLE`.
- [ ] Hệ thống tạo LoyaltyTransaction `REDEEMED`.

## Acceptance Criteria
**FR-AS-14:**

Customer nhận voucher và active points giảm đúng.

## PR Merge Gate
PR có thể được merge nếu:
- [ ] Code build/run được.
- [ ] PR liên quan trực tiếp đến grouped issue này.
- [ ] Các checklist chính của issue đã hoàn thành hoặc phần chưa làm được ghi rõ là follow-up.
- [ ] Không phá chức năng hiện có.
- [ ] Đã có ít nhất 2 reviewer theo quy định review của nhóm.
- [ ] PR phải sử dụng đúng Pull Request template trong thư mục `.github` (ví dụ: `.github/pull_request_template.md`).
- [ ] PR description không được để trống.
- [ ] PR phải link issue liên quan bằng cú pháp như `Closes #43`, `Fixes #43`, hoặc `Related to #43`.
- [ ] PR phải điền đầy đủ các phần chính trong template, gồm summary, changes, testing hoặc manual test note, checklist.
> **Note:** Agent review sẽ yêu cầu sửa PR description nếu PR không dùng template hoặc để trống phần bắt buộc.

## Merge Blockers
PR không được merge nếu có lỗi nghiêm trọng trong issue này.
- Redeem reward bằng điểm đã hết hạn. Đổi voucher thành công nhưng không bị trừ điểm.
> **Note:** Hardcode business/display values chỉ ghi warning, không tự động block merge (trừ khi làm sai checklist hoặc sai nghiệp vụ). PR quá scope issue chỉ ghi warning/tư vấn tách PR, không tự động block merge nếu không phá chức năng.

`createPaymentIntent()` returns `payload.currency` exactly as submitted. Mixed-case or whitespace-padded values such as `" USD "` are returned as non-canonical payment intent currency values, while payment providers typically expect normalized lowercase ISO currency codes.

title: IContentPack.h references a GOVERNANCE.md linking-exception text that doesn't exist
body_excerpt:
## Problem

The header comment on `engine/content/IContentPack.h` states:

> Linking exception: content pack implementors (mods, plugins) may link against this header without being required to license their work under GPL v3. **See GOVERNANCE.md for the full exception text.**

`GOVERNANCE.md` contains no linking-exception text — nothing matching "exception" appears in the file. The one-sentence summary in the header is currently the only statement of the exception anywhere in the repository.

## Why it matters

- The exception is load-bearing for the content-pack ecosystem: it is what allows non-GPL plugins to implement `IContentPack` (the engine's distribution docs have positioned fa-bridge as possibly paid/non-GPL on exactly this basis).
- fa-bridge's distribution/licensing decision ([fa-bridge#37](https://github.com/fighters-legacy/fa-bridge/issues/37)) leans on this exception being well-defined; a dangling reference weakens it.
- There is no standard SPDX identifier for a custom linking exception, so the authoritative text has to live somewhere in-repo — the header promises GOVERNANCE.md delivers it.

## Fix

Write the full exception text (scope: which headers it covers — the vendorable interface set `IContentPack.h`, `AssetTypes.h`, `TrustLevel.h`; what "link against" permits; what remains GPL) into GOVERNANCE.md, or move it to a dedicated `LICENSES/`/`LICENSE-EXCEPTION` file and update the header comment's pointer.

title: find NOW-DEBT: principal on query-facts (QueryFactRecorder cross-instance leak) — blocks self-history axis
body_excerpt:
Surfaced by two adversarial reviews of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-find-shared-core-convergence-claim.md`.

`QueryFactRecorder` writes every query under a single fixed `QUERY_PROVIDER_ID = uuid5(..., "yanantin.query.service")` with **no principal on the fact** (`src/yanantin/query/recorder.py:20,42`). Its docstring advertises cross-instance pattern detection. So 'what did **I** find' = 'what did **everyone** find' — a shipped yanantin#13 violation.

This is a NOW-DEBT, not a deferrable seam: every unattributed query-fact written now is data #13 must later retrofit identity onto (commons→isolation is the irreversible direction). The meta-recursion (queries-as-activity-data as a self-history axis) MUST NOT be leaned on until this is paid.

**Done =** query-facts carry principal-shaped attribution + a red-bar test that goes red if a query-fact is written without a principal. Joined to #13.

## Scope
- [ ] `GET/POST /catalog`: Parent creation with title and CC price 0 < price ≤ 100 000, immediately redeemable (Req 11.1, 11.9); exemption-day flag (Req 11.8)
- [ ] Entry state machine proposed/redeemable/rejected/retired per design.md §3.1; only redeemable entries can be redeemed (Req 11.5)
- [ ] `PATCH /catalog/{id}` price edit: recalculate affected goal targets and notify every holder (Req 11.6, 12.6)
- [ ] `POST /catalog/{id}/retire`: holders' goals marked inactive, allocation released, re-choose prompt event emitted (Req 11.6, 12.6)
- [ ] Family-wide semantics: no per-child entries or prices (Req 11.7)
- [ ] Pending Redemptions keep their captured price across price changes (Req 14.7)
- [ ] P2 proposal endpoints (child create, approve, reject) namespace-reserved, returning `404 feature_disabled` (design.md §4.1)

## Acceptance criteria
- Integration tests: a price edit updates each holder's goal target and creates a `catalog.entry_changed` notification per holder (Req 11.6, 12.6)
- Retirement marks holders' goals inactive and releases their allocations (Req 12.6)
- Price of 0, negative, or above 100 000 rejected 422 with the field named (Req 11.9, NFR-8.3)
- Default-deny tests: Child catalog mutations denied; P2 proposal routes return `404 feature_disabled`
- A pending Redemption completes at its captured price after a price edit (Req 14.7)

## References
- Requirements: Req 11.1, Req 11.5–11.9, Req 12.6, Req 14.7, NFR-8.3
- Design: design.md §3.1, §4.1, §4.2

title: ## 🟠 P1 — #565 · `overfit_gap`-Asymmetrie belohnt OOS-Glück; keine Fold-Dispersions-Strafe
body_excerpt:
**Symptom.** Eligible Trials haben `overfit_gap = 0`, d. h. `is_sortino_median ≤ base(=5)`. Der annualisierte OOS-Sortino (≥5, geklemmt) liegt **über** dem IS-Median — ein Muster, das typisch für ein **glückliches OOS-Sub-Fenster** ist und auf dem Holdout revertiert (`R_symbol ≈ −5.1`). Die Reward-Funktion gibt dafür **vollen Kredit**.

**Root-Cause (Mathematik).** `overfit_gap = max(0, is_sortino_median − base)` bestraft ausschließlich `IS > OOS`. Der Fall `OOS ≫ IS` (Overfit auf ein günstiges Fenster) wird mit `gap = 0` **nicht** bestraft. Zusätzlich fließt in den Reward der **gepoolte/Median-** OOS-Sortino, nicht die **Streuung** über die Folds — ein einzelner starker Fold kann den Wert tragen (die Fold-Konsistenz greift nur im Gate über `oos_min_profitable_folds_frac`, nicht im Reward).

**Fix.**
1. **Symmetrische Divergenz-Strafe** statt einseitigem Overfit-Gap:
   ```
   divergence_pen = w_of · |is_sortino_median − base|
   ```
   Ein großer Betrag in *beide* Richtungen signalisiert Instabilität IS↔OOS. Optional asymmetrisch gewichtet (`OOS≫IS` etwas milder, aber ungleich 0).
2. **Fold-Dispersions-Strafe** in den Reward heben: Streuung der Per-Fold-OOS-Sortinos (`collect_oos_fold_sortinos` existiert bereits, `backtest_runner.py:816`) als Malus:
   ```
   reward −= w_disp · pstdev(per_fold_oos_sortino)
   ```
   Belohnt *konsistente* statt *glücklicher* Performance und ist die Reward-seitige Ergänzung zum Gate-seitigen #550.
3. **Deflated Sortino** (#553, aktuell `deflated_selection=false`) als Winner-Kriterium aktivieren (siehe #568): kontrolliert die False-Positive-Winner-Rate gegen das Rausch-Maximum über N Konfigurationen — genau der Selection-Bias, der hier zuschlägt.

**Akzeptanzkriterien.**
- Property-Test: bei `OOS_sortino = 5`, `IS_median = 1` ist `reward` messbar niedriger als bei `OOS = IS = 5` (OOS-Glück wird bestraft).
- Fold-Dispersion wirkt: zwei Trials mit gleichem Median-OOS-Sortino, aber unterschiedlicher Fold-Streuung, erhalten unterschiedlichen Reward (niedrigere Streuung → höher).
- A/B auf `TSLA.ETORO`: mittlerer Holdout-Regret sinkt gegenüber Baseline.

**Betroffene Dateien.** `automation/optimizer/reward.py` (`compute_reward` — `divergence_pen`, `fold_dispersion_pen`), `automation/optimizer/parsing.py` (Fold-Sortino-Streuung in `TournamentMetrics` durchreichen, falls nicht vorhanden), `automation/tests/test_issue_566_overfit_symmetry.py` (neu).

title: v0.2 launch defaults — pricing / domain / landing copy (vote with reactions)

## Help me lock the v0.2 launch defaults

Three things I've been chewing on and don't want to lock alone. Reactions on the bullet points below count as a vote (👍 for "ship this one"). Comments welcome if "actually do X instead" — those override reactions.

### Q1 — Pricing entry

What should the first 60 days of v0.2 look like?

- 🟢 **Free + email collect.** Build a list, ship Stage 2 paid tier once it's >100 emails.
- 🚀 **PWYW $0+ tip jar.** Same flow as free, but tip-jar conversion data is the only revenue signal.
- 💸 **$7/month from day one.** Matches Mailbutler middle tier ($7), Streak / Mixmax / Instantly start higher ($15–$59).
- 🎯 **$5 one-time unlock CSV download (free preview top 20).** Lower friction than monthly, no churn risk.

### Q2 — Domain

Working names so far. I'll register whichever wins:

- 👀 **`coldthreads.app`** — direct, "what it does"
- 👍 **`inboxintel.so`** — tool-flavored, ties to project name
- ❤️ **`silentthreads.app`** — abstract, leans on the metaphor
- 🎉 **Other (comment)** — toss a name; if it survives review I'll buy that one

### Q3 — Landing copy (1-line value prop)

Whichever lands at the top of `app/page.tsx`. Currently A is shipped in preview.

- 👍 **A: "See which client emails went cold this week."** Outcome-first, specific time-window.
- 🚀 **B: "Your inbox knows which leads ghosted you. Show me."** More conversational, slightly more SaaS-y.
- ❤️ **C: "30 seconds to find the 5 client threads you forgot."** Quantified, time-claim risk.

### How to vote

React to the bullets above with the emoji at the start of each line. No comment required.

Comments override reactions if you have a strong case. Comments without a vote are also welcome — context > tally.

Spec lives in [upstream Discussion #16](https://github.com/foxck016077/apify-gmail-inbox-intel/discussions/16) if you want the long-form context, including the competitor scan and what's already shipped vs blocked.

I'll lock these once any one of the three sees a clear lead, or in 14 days, whichever is sooner.

title: Add subscription functionality (decide: keep stx-static or convert to a Stacks app)
body_excerpt:
## Context

Per Chris's 2026-05-07 11:36 AM task drop:

> "add a subscription functionality to pawel dregans site (however easiest within our setup there and in aws, maybe actually deploy it as a stacks app instead of a stx one)"

The site is currently a static stx site (built via `bun run build` → static HTML, no DB / no server runtime). Adding subscription functionality (email capture → mailing list, or paid recurring subscription, or both — needs clarification) means we have a fork in the road:

- **Option A — keep stx static**, add a serverless backend for subscriptions only (Lambda + API Gateway + DynamoDB or SES, etc.). Site stays cheap and CDN-served; only the subscribe endpoint is dynamic.
- **Option B — convert paweldregan to a Stacks app**, deployed via our standard Stacks deploy flow. Gives us DB, email, sessions, payments surface for free. Heavier ops footprint, but sets the precedent for `pet-store` (which will need the same surface).

Chris's hint leans toward B *"maybe actually deploy it as a stacks app instead of a stx one"* — but it's a hint, not a decision.

## Decision needed (before any implementation)

1. **What kind of subscription?** Email-list opt-in only, or paid recurring (newsletter / coaching slots / training plans)? Different scope.
2. **A or B?** If we expect `pet-store` to need the same backend stack, doing B here first is a useful dry run. If subscription is just an email opt-in, A is way cheaper.
3. **Email destination:** if it's a mailing list, where does it land? blocked by [#7](https://github.com/stacksjs/paweldregan/issues/7) (mail-os multi-domain setup for `hello@paweldregan.com`).

## Acceptance

- Decision documented in this issue thread.
- If A: Lambda + storage + email plumbing in place; subscribe endpoint reachable; opt-in confirmed working end-to-end against a real address.
- If B: paweldregan migrated to a Stacks app with the same public-facing pages + the new subscribe surface; deployed; existing SEO/og/i18n behavior preserved (don't regress [#5](https://github.com/stacksjs/paweldregan/issues/5)).

## Related

- [#7](https://github.com/stacksjs/paweldregan/issues/7) — mail infra (likely a hard prereq for any email-driven subscription).
- [#10](https://github.com/stacksjs/paweldregan/issues/10) — analytics rollout (unrelated, but if we go option B we should make sure analytics still works through the Stacks app surface).

title: Go-to-market & monetization strategy (living plan)
