## Purpose

Living home for Wardnet's **go-to-market and monetization strategy**. This is a tracking/discussion issue, not a code task — it captures the durable commitments and the evolving execution plan. The engineering work it implies is tracked in #609 (premium tier + entitlement) and #610 (bridge decoupling).

## Durable commitments (decided — see `docs/adr-premium-tier-and-entitlement.md`)

- **Free tier is the growth engine and is permanently free.** Self-host + bring-your-own-domain = full features, zero cost to us. Premium never gates the self-hostable product.
- **Premium gates a real cost centre** (DDNS + Tunneler run on our infra), so it is paid **from public availability** — never given away free and later charged for (clawback is the cardinal sin).
- **Beta is free but explicitly labelled** "free during beta → premium at GA, with advance notice." Never silently free.
- **Stripe-native trial at GA.** Stripe is the payment processor only; the account master record is ours (tenant management).
- **Positioning: transparent-but-quiet.** Free/self-hostable product and the mission are the hero; premium is an honest, secondary "supports the project" tier. The solo-OSS identity is a trust asset, leaned into — not a slick SaaS launch.

- [ ] Launch copy + the explicit beta-pricing notice wording

Solo + pre-launch: Discussions earn their keep when there's a community conversing. This repo standardized on issues (impl-docs retired in favour of issues, d8ed6c83), so a long-lived `strategy`-labelled issue is the idiomatic home. Revisit if/when a public community forms.

title: CostTracker governance gaps: WARN overrun is silent, OBSERVE waives new-paid-tool approval, approved tools lost on resume
body_excerpt:
**Category:** Bug — budget-governance contract violations (\`tools/cost_tracker.py\`)

Three related defects in \`reserve()\` and persistence undermine the spend-governance contract that AGENT_GUIDE.md leans on.

**1. WARN mode never signals a budget overrun** — \`tools/cost_tracker.py:143-148\`
\`\`\`python
if estimated > self.usable_budget_usd:
    if self.mode == BudgetMode.CAP:
        raise BudgetExceededError(...)
# WARN falls straight through and reserves — no log, no flag, no return signal
\`\`\`
The module docstring promises "Budget overruns trigger pauses (in warn/cap mode)." In WARN mode an overrun produces **nothing** the orchestrator can detect. Fix: emit \`logging.warning(...)\` and/or set \`entry["budget_warning"] = True\` (surfaced in \`cost_snapshot()\`).

**2. \`BudgetMode.OBSERVE\` silently waives BOTH approval gates** — \`tools/cost_tracker.py:127-140\`
The single-action-threshold check (127) and the new-paid-tool check (135) are both gated on \`self.mode != BudgetMode.OBSERVE\`. So \`require_approval_for_new_paid_tool=True\` becomes a no-op the moment mode is OBSERVE, and a brand-new paid provider runs unapproved. Spend-cap mode and consent are orthogonal and should not be coupled. Fix: keep new-paid-tool / single-action approval active regardless of budget mode (or add a separate flag).

**3. \`_approved_tools\` is not persisted — resume re-prompts for already-approved tools** — \`tools/cost_tracker.py:59, 155-157\`, \`_save()/_load()\`
\`_approved_tools\` is an in-memory \`set\` never written by \`_save()\` nor restored by \`_load()\`. On any pipeline resume (a fresh \`CostTracker\` built from an existing \`cost_log.json\`), every previously approved paid tool is forgotten and \`reserve()\` raises \`ApprovalRequiredError\` again — breaking resumability of paid stages. Fix: persist approved tool names in the saved JSON and rehydrate in \`_load()\`.

title: Logical Reasoning with Outcome Reward Models for Test-Time Scaling
body_excerpt:
**Paper**: [Logical Reasoning with Outcome Reward Models for Test-Time Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19903v1)

## TL;DR

Paper trains Outcome Reward Models for deductive text-LLM reasoning + test-time scaling. Repo is inference-only VLM spatial-reasoning eval — no trainer, no reward-model path, no logic benchmark, no scoped call site. Decide fit.

## Suggested experiment

Scope a test-time-selection harness that fits the existing inference-only path: for each spatial-reasoning benchmark item, have the VLM generate N candidate answers, score each with a lightweight proxy reward (reuse `evaluation.py`'s ground-truth scoring as a stand-in for a learned ORM), and measure the accuracy lift from best-of-N selection over the single-shot baseline. This tests whether ORM-style test-time scaling transfers to the spatial VLM setting before investing in training a real reward model.

## Engineering analysis

The paper contributes three things, all centered on **text LLMs doing deductive logic**:

- A set of trained **Outcome Reward Models (ORMs)** that score whether an LLM's reasoning trace reaches a correct conclusion on deductive-reasoning tasks.
- A **training recipe** for those ORMs (needs a trainer, supervised/RL data, and a model head).
- A **test-time scaling recipe**: generate N candidate reasoning traces, score each with the ORM, select the best.

This is fundamentally an LLM logical-reasoning method: text in, text out, built on a reward-modeling + training pipeline.

### What blocks a clean implementation

- **Modality and domain mismatch.** vqasynth is an **inference + evaluation pipeline for visual spatial reasoning** over VLMs (`benchmarks.py`, `evaluation.py`, `inference.py`, plus `depth`/`localize`/`scene_fusion`). The paper targets **deductive logical reasoning** over text LLMs. There is no logical-reasoning benchmark, no text-only LLM path, and no spatial ↔ deductive bridge in the repo.
- **No training infrastructure.** The paper's core contribution is *training* ORMs and *selecting among candidates via reward scores*. vqasynth is inference-only — there is no trainer, no reward-model head, and no candidate-generate + score + select harness. `r1_reasoning.py` does reasoning prompting but not ORM-scored best-of-N selection.
- **No scoped call site identified.** No candidate-selection rationale named a subset or call site against this module layout, so there is no implementable slice that drops into existing code. The most realistic implementation
